speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether he can elaborate on how our pandemic preparedness plan has been updated to include large-scale influenza outbreaks; (b) specifically, what measures are in place to handle a sudden spike in infections; and (c) how does the Ministry ensure sufficient healthcare capacity during such surges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Our public hospitals treat high patient volumes on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In light of recent influenza outbreaks in regional countries, such as Thailand, what steps is the Ministry taking to enhance influenza vaccination coverage amongst the high-risk populations in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For instance, in Yio Chu Kang, we work with donors and clinics to provide free flu vaccinations for seniors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And how are these strategies informed by lessons learnt from COVID-19 vaccination roll-outs?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This is something that we have to think about on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: You have to update your vaccinations on a regular basis.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Similarly, this is something that anyone who is in regular contact with seniors as a result of the service that they are offering, such as the examples that Mr Yip provided in his constituency, can and should ask seniors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Even on a personal level for family members, children can very often play an important role in reminding their parents.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, for me, for example, for many years, I have had the habit of using my parents' wedding anniversary as a marker in my calendar to nag them, gently nudge them.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And then, as they have now become a little bit older, I take on the responsibility of making the appointment for them to then go and receive their influenza vaccinations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, from an organisational, a social and a personal level, we can often find ways to constantly remind the seniors amongst us above the age of 65 that a regular influenza vaccination would be a very important part of protecting themselves.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In parallel, the good social habits, the personal hygiene that I mentioned in my original Parliamentary Question answer also need to continue to be reinforced.
